pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: ACTIVE AND PASSIVE VOICE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.3: Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should one use a variety of sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify sentences in the active and passive voice
2. construct sentences in the active and passive voice
3. appreciate the use of active and passive voice in effective communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice

Teach
• Focus skill: identify sentences in the active and passive voice.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should one use a variety of sentences?
2. How can one tell the doer and the receiver of an action in a sentence?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
